::: {.callout-note}
## Practice designing a focused experiment

1. Choose a verified gap with a measurable baseline and target.
2. Describe one change and the result you expect from it.
3. Break the test into small action steps and assign one owner.
4. Move the experiment to verification only after collecting evidence.
:::

## Example experiment

| Attribute | Example |
|---|---|
| Experiment title | Reduce intake data errors |
| Target gap | Data error rate: 8% baseline → 3% target |
| Hypothesis | If we add a required-field check at intake, then data error rate will improve by 5 percentage points. |
| Action steps | Define required fields; pilot the check for one week; review rejected records |
| Owner | Intake coordinator |
| Success metric | Data error rate at or below 3% during the pilot |
| Priority | High |
| Status | Backlog / Proposed |

Keep the hypothesis specific enough to disprove. A completed action is not evidence of improvement; compare the observed success metric with the baseline and target before marking an experiment completed.

## Try your own roadmap

Export `gap-analysis.csv` from Gap Analysis, then import it into the workspace. Critical or high gaps become starting cards that you can edit in either board or table view.
